title: Maximum Product of the Length of Two Palindromic Subsequences
summary: Given a string, identify two non-overlapping palindromic subsequences whose combined length product is maximized.
statement: Given a string, identify two non-overlapping palindromic subsequences whose combined length product is maximized. Return this maximum product. A subsequence is formed by deleting characters from the original string while maintaining the order of the remaining characters. A string is palindromic if it remains the same when read backward.
constraints: Choose two nonempty subsequences using disjoint character indices, and require both to be palindromes.
Return the maximum product of their lengths.
hints: With at most twelve positions, bitmasks can enumerate every subsequence exactly.
Precompute which masks form palindromes, then enumerate palindrome masks inside each complement.
For palindrome first, iterate all subsets of full^first and maximize popcount products for palindrome second.
Complement restriction is exactly disjointness, and exhaustive mask enumeration includes every legal pair.
editorial: Complement restriction is exactly disjointness, and exhaustive mask enumeration includes every legal pair.
